en.greeting: Hi! You know how to say what's happening now: I'm cooking. Today we take it into the past: I was cooking. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: Sedang, but in the past
steps.text: You already say what's happening now: I'm cooking. What about something that was happening last night?
steps.body: Change **am/is/are** to **was/were** and keep the **-ing**: *I'm cooking* (now) → **At 8 last night I was cooking.** This is the **past continuous**: an action **in progress** (started, not finished yet) at a time in the past. Indonesian keeps the same *sedang* and only adds a time word (*jam 8 tadi malam saya sedang memasak*). English changes the helper word too: 'At 8 last night I am cooking' ✗ → **I was cooking**. And keep the -ing: 'I was cook' ✗.

pairs.id: Saya sedang memasak. (tadi, di masa lalu)

steps.title: In the middle at 8
steps.text: Picture last night. Where is 8 o'clock?

timeline.title: Last night: cooking dinner
timeline.caption: You started cooking at 7:30 and finished at 8:30. At 8 you were in the middle: I was cooking. was/were + -ing = in the middle of an action at that moment.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Put Indonesian 'sedang' into the past.

question.prompt: Which sentence means 'Jam 8 tadi malam Rina sedang membuat kue'?
options: At 8 last night Rina is making a cake.
At 8 last night Rina was making a cake.
At 8 last night Rina was make a cake.
question.explanation: **8 last night** is in the past, so **is** becomes **was**, and the verb keeps -ing: **Rina was making a cake.** 'is making' keeps the present (the *sedang* habit), and 'was make' drops the -ing.

steps.title: was or were?
steps.text: It's the same choice you know from the past of to be.
steps.body: **I, he, she, it** and one person (*Rina, my boss*) → **was**. **you, we, they** and two or more (*my parents, Budi and Sari*) → **were**. 'They was' ✗: *they* is more than one, so **they were**. **you** is always **were**, even for one person (because it's *you are*). Indonesian has no was/were, so check the **subject** (who does the action). Spell the -ing as before: *have → having* (drop the e), *run → running* (double), *study → studying*.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Saturday afternoon at home.

question.prompt: Complete: At four yesterday afternoon, my sisters ___ the car.
question.explanation: **my sisters** = they (two or more) → **were**, plus the -ing: **were washing**. 'was' is only for one person or thing, and 'were wash' is missing the -ing.

steps.title: At 9 last night
steps.text: At 9 last night, at Sari's house, everyone was in the middle of something.
steps.body: One person or thing → **was**; two or more → **were**. In *It was raining*, **it** means nothing: English just needs a word at the start, as in *It's raining*.

examples.en: Sari was doing her homework.
examples.id: Sari sedang mengerjakan PR-nya.

examples.en: Her father was reading the news on his phone.
examples.id: Ayahnya sedang membaca berita di HP-nya.

examples.en: Her mother was talking to Bu Ani on the phone.
examples.id: Ibunya sedang mengobrol dengan Bu Ani di telepon.

examples.en: Her grandparents were sitting on the terrace.
examples.id: Kakek dan neneknya sedang duduk di teras.

examples.en: It was raining outside.
examples.id: Di luar sedang hujan.

steps.title: Not, and questions
steps.text: Negatives and questions work just like was/were on their own.
steps.body: **Negative:** **wasn't / weren't** + -ing: *I wasn't sleeping.* **Question:** **Was/Were** first, then the subject: *He was eating* → **Was he eating?** Short answers: **Yes, he was. / No, he wasn't.** To ask about a time: **What were you doing at 8?** No **did** here (was/were already shows the past): 'Did you sleeping?' ✗. And don't just add a question mark: 'You were sleeping?' → **Were you sleeping?**

pairs.en: Yes, he was. / No, he wasn't.

steps.title: Build the question
steps.text: You want to know what your friend Rina was doing on the phone.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Apakah dia (perempuan) sedang menelepon ibunya?
question.explanation: Question = **Was/Were** + subject + -ing: **Was she calling her mother?** *she* is one person → **Was**, not Were. No *did*: was already shows the past.

steps.title: Listen and answer
steps.text: Your colleague Budi asks you something. Press play and listen.

question.listen: What were you doing at three yesterday afternoon?
question.prompt: Listen to Budi's question. Choose the best answer.
options: I'm reading a book in my room.
I was reading a book in my room.
question.explanation: Budi asks **What were you doing at three yesterday afternoon?** A past time + *what … doing* asks what you were in the middle of → **I was reading a book in my room.** 'Yes, I was' only answers a yes/no question (*Were you…?*), and 'I'm reading' is about now.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip through these cards to lock in was/were + -ing.

flashcards.front: Jam 8 tadi malam saya sedang memasak.
flashcards.back: At 8 last night I was cooking.
Rina wasn't laughing. (Rina tidak sedang tertawa.)
Were you working? (Apakah kamu sedang bekerja?)

flashcards.front: Kamu sedang apa jam 10 tadi malam?
flashcards.back: What were you doing at 10 last night?
They were watching TV. ✓ (Mereka sedang menonton TV.)

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for later.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · past continuous
artifact.intro: was/were + -ing: what was in progress at a time in the past.
tips: **was/were + -ing** = in the middle of an action at a past time: **At 8 last night I was cooking.**
One person or thing → **was**; you / two or more → **were**. Never 'they was'.
A past time + *sedang* → was/were, not am/is/are: 'At 8 last night I am cooking' ✗. No did in questions: **Were you sleeping?**

examples.en: At 6 this morning I was waiting for an ojek.
examples.id: Jam 6 tadi pagi saya sedang menunggu ojek.

examples.en: My friends were having lunch in the kantin at one.
examples.id: Teman-temanku sedang makan siang di kantin jam satu.

examples.en: Was it raining in Bogor? — Yes, it was.
examples.id: Apakah di Bogor sedang hujan? — Ya.

examples.en: What were you doing at 10 last night? — I was watching a film.
examples.id: Kamu sedang apa jam 10 tadi malam? — Saya sedang menonton film.

examples.en: Last night I cooked dinner. At 8 I was cooking.
examples.id: Tadi malam saya memasak makan malam (selesai). Jam 8 saya sedang memasak.

id.greeting: Hai! Kamu sudah bisa bilang apa yang sedang terjadi sekarang: I'm cooking. Hari ini kita bawa ke masa lalu: I was cooking. Ayo kita pelajari pelan-pelan.

steps.title: Sedang, tapi di masa lalu
steps.text: Kamu sudah bisa bilang apa yang sedang terjadi sekarang: I'm cooking. Bagaimana dengan kegiatan yang sedang berlangsung tadi malam?
steps.body: Ganti **am/is/are** dengan **was/were**, dan -ing-nya tetap: *I'm cooking* (sekarang) → **At 8 last night I was cooking.** Ini namanya **past continuous**: kegiatan yang **sedang berlangsung** (sudah dimulai, belum selesai) pada suatu waktu di masa lalu. Bahasa Indonesia tetap memakai *sedang* dan hanya menambah kata waktu (*jam 8 tadi malam saya sedang memasak*). Bahasa Inggris juga mengubah kata bantunya: 'At 8 last night I am cooking' ✗ → **I was cooking**. Dan -ing-nya jangan dibuang: 'I was cook' ✗.

pairs.id: Saya sedang memasak. (tadi, di masa lalu)

steps.title: Di tengah kegiatan jam 8
steps.text: Bayangkan tadi malam. Jam 8 ada di mana?

timeline.title: Tadi malam: memasak makan malam
timeline.caption: Kamu mulai memasak jam 7.30 dan selesai jam 8.30. Jam 8 kamu sedang di tengah kegiatan itu: I was cooking. was/were + -ing = sedang di tengah sebuah kegiatan pada saat itu.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Ubah 'sedang' ke masa lalu.

question.prompt: Kalimat mana yang artinya 'Jam 8 tadi malam Rina sedang membuat kue'?
options: At 8 last night Rina is making a cake.
At 8 last night Rina was making a cake.
At 8 last night Rina was make a cake.
question.explanation: **8 last night** sudah lewat, jadi **is** menjadi **was**, dan kata kerjanya tetap -ing: **Rina was making a cake.** 'is making' tetap bentuk sekarang (kebiasaan dari kata *sedang*), dan 'was make' kehilangan -ing.

steps.title: was atau were?
steps.text: Pilihannya sama seperti yang kamu kenal dari bentuk lampau to be.
steps.body: **I, he, she, it** dan satu orang (*Rina, my boss*) → **was**. **you, we, they** dan dua orang atau lebih (*my parents, Budi and Sari*) → **were**. 'They was' ✗: *they* lebih dari satu, jadi **they were**. **you** selalu **were**, walaupun satu orang (karena *you are*). Bahasa Indonesia tidak punya was/were, jadi selalu cek **subjeknya** (siapa yang melakukan). Ejaan -ing sama seperti sebelumnya: *have → having* (buang e), *run → running* (gandakan), *study → studying*.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Sabtu sore di rumah.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: At four yesterday afternoon, my sisters ___ the car.
question.explanation: **my sisters** = they (dua orang atau lebih) → **were**, ditambah -ing: **were washing**. 'was' hanya untuk satu orang atau benda, dan 'were wash' tidak memakai -ing.

steps.title: Jam 9 tadi malam
steps.text: Jam 9 tadi malam, di rumah Sari, semua orang sedang melakukan sesuatu.
steps.body: Satu orang atau benda → **was**; dua atau lebih → **were**. Di *It was raining*, **it** tidak ada artinya: bahasa Inggris cuma butuh kata di depan, sama seperti *It's raining*.

examples.en: Sari was doing her homework.
examples.id: Sari sedang mengerjakan PR-nya.

examples.en: Her father was reading the news on his phone.
examples.id: Ayahnya sedang membaca berita di HP-nya.

examples.en: Her mother was talking to Bu Ani on the phone.
examples.id: Ibunya sedang mengobrol dengan Bu Ani di telepon.

examples.en: Her grandparents were sitting on the terrace.
examples.id: Kakek dan neneknya sedang duduk di teras.

examples.en: It was raining outside.
examples.id: Di luar sedang hujan.

steps.title: Negatif dan pertanyaan
steps.text: Kalimat negatif dan pertanyaan caranya sama seperti was/were tanpa kata kerja lain.
steps.body: **Negatif:** **wasn't / weren't** + -ing: *I wasn't sleeping.* **Pertanyaan:** **Was/Were** di depan, lalu subjeknya: *He was eating* → **Was he eating?** Jawaban singkat: **Yes, he was. / No, he wasn't.** Untuk bertanya tentang suatu jam: **What were you doing at 8?** Di sini tidak pakai **did** (was/were sudah menunjukkan masa lalu): 'Did you sleeping?' ✗. Dan jangan hanya menambah tanda tanya: 'You were sleeping?' → **Were you sleeping?**

pairs.en: Yes, he was. / No, he wasn't.

steps.title: Susun pertanyaannya
steps.text: Kamu ingin tahu apa yang sedang dilakukan temanmu Rina di telepon.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Apakah dia (perempuan) sedang menelepon ibunya?
question.explanation: Pertanyaan = **Was/Were** + subjek + -ing: **Was she calling her mother?** *she* satu orang → **Was**, bukan Were. Tanpa *did*: was sudah menunjukkan masa lalu.

steps.title: Dengar dan jawab
steps.text: Rekan kerjamu Budi menanyakan sesuatu. Tekan play dan dengarkan.

question.listen: What were you doing at three yesterday afternoon?
question.prompt: Dengarkan pertanyaan Budi. Pilih jawaban yang paling tepat.
options: I'm reading a book in my room.
I was reading a book in my room.
question.explanation: Budi bertanya **What were you doing at three yesterday afternoon?** Waktu lampau + *what … doing* menanyakan kegiatan yang sedang kamu lakukan saat itu → **I was reading a book in my room.** 'Yes, I was' hanya menjawab pertanyaan ya/tidak (*Were you…?*), dan 'I'm reading' tentang sekarang.

steps.title: Ulangan cepat
steps.text: Balik kartu-kartu ini supaya was/were + -ing makin melekat.

Were you working? (Apakah kamu sedang bekerja?)

flashcards.back: What were you doing at 10 last night?
They were watching TV. ✓ (Mereka sedang menonton TV.)
